text:
HR@10 with one positive and 99 sampled negatives measures success within a 100-item candidate set, not full-catalog retrieval. Sampled metrics can reverse model rankings even in expectation; fixed candidates improve comparability but do not remove sampling bias ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). With 200 users/category, one hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and four-category macro HR by 0.125 points. Repeated checkpoint and architecture selection on those same users creates optimistic selection bias; disclose all trials, checkpoint-selection rules and validation queries, and label selected validation gains exploratory. Freeze the final procedure before the host’s held-out evaluation ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)).

Recommended comparison: evaluate baseline NextItNet, [h,u] gates and [h,u,e_t] gates on identical users and candidate sets. Report each category’s hit counts, HR@10, paired absolute differences, and discordant counts: users gained versus users lost. Include both gates versus baseline and [h,u,e_t] versus [h,u]. Use paired-user bootstrap confidence intervals; exact McNemar tests can assess paired binary outcomes. Prespecify contrasts and adjust multiple comparisons, while acknowledging that adjustment does not erase adaptive validation reuse ([paired bootstrap](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html), [McNemar](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman1/auxillar/mcnemar.htm)).

For macro uncertainty, resample users within each category, retaining all three models’ outcomes together, then average the four category differences with equal weights in every replicate. Report 95% intervals alongside category effects. These intervals condition on fitted seed-42 models, fixed candidates and these four categories; they exclude training-seed variability, candidate-resampling variability and selection bias. One seed supports claims about these fitted models, not robust architecture superiority or generalization across domains.
